Lens: acceptance by tron maintainers. Facts verified at /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-attn-stats (HEAD is now 9b3832eb4b on top of 66c7bb8db1, branch jhan-attn-path-stats, clean; no PR opened yet: `gh pr list --head jhan-attn-path-stats` = []).

(1) The reviewers asked for exactly this shape. PR #4267 (page-share counters, compile-time option) was approved by Wado-posi (review 5156698046, 2026-09-09: "Collection could still be opt-in (via env-var maybe), then they could be inspected live and measured over random chosen intervals") and by bgamari-positron (review 5160920121). Issue #4303 (OPEN, 2026-09-10, no comments) records that ask with the prerequisite "an A/A control benchmark ... showing that the counting code, compiled into every build but switched off by the environment variable, costs nothing measurable", and its Done-when item has the two-way branch (a) option removed / (b) option kept if acceptance fails. The earlier objection to instrumentation "compiled by nobody" (memory wade-fuse-question-pr4267.md:39: a relayed Claude review on #3879; the GitHub text was not found in the #3879 reviews/comments API: unverified) is an objection to default-OFF build options. A CMake option in this PR therefore contradicts two approving reviewers and re-opens that objection; an env var satisfies both.

(2) The in-tree precedent for hot-path counters is compile-time and both instances are recent: TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS (CMakeLists.txt:47, f6794a7c15 by jhan 2026-09-04, ON only in the coverage preset CMakePresets.json:119) and TRON_MWAIT_STATS (src/system/CMakeLists.txt:36, c03347b1fc by rbjarnason 2026-09-22 "Disable wait statistics by default", CMakePresets.json:120). The PR must name both and give the reason for departing: the reviewers' ask plus the measured OFF cost. Always-compiled run-time-gated precedents exist at the same loop: the perfetto TRACE_EVENT at the top of every apply_page_range call (HEAD self_attention.hpp:1391) and the 8 unconditional rdtsc reads per job in run_attention_job (:774-806).

(3) Cost margin makes a build option indefensible on review: the OFF path is one bool copied per apply_page_range call and one `if (stats_on)` per visit (diff: 4 lines at entry, 4 after the apply_page_tok call, 6 at the end, placed as siblings of the PAGE_SHARE #ifdef blocks); apply_page_tok is TRON(inline) = always_inline (h/common/attributes.hpp:78; 0 apply_page_tok symbols in the 8fd1e7798d runtron, 472 apply_page_range instantiations), so the path tag never crosses a call boundary; 1-2 cycles per visit against 5,800-9,300 cycles per dense visit (Table 2, prompt ~1100) = 60-400x below the 116-465 cycles that would cost 1 % TPS. The M1 A/A can only certify "not obvious" (< ~1 %); the instruction-count delta is the deterministic companion.

(4) Review-sensitive items in the commit and how they read: return-type change of apply_page_tok = pair -> named struct page_tok_result {hint, relevant_k_tokens, served} with static_assert(sizeof == sizeof(pair) && trivially copyable) (self_attention.hpp:1771-1781), 2 callers only (self_attention.hpp:1596, t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2394-2398): a readability refactor, acceptable. shared_ptr<model_stats> in self_attention::state (:469): one allocation per model state, rows/fpga vectors empty when off (attn_stats.hpp:248-251), required because runtron destroys states while the FUSE tree is mounted (stream_generate.hpp:1009 vs runtron.cpp:485) so the leaves must hold a weak_ptr; acceptable with that sentence in the comment (present at :466-468). JSON string leaves: precedent expert_stats.hpp:181-196; casual leaves outside /exported carry no convention obligation (README.stats.md:224-228, fuse_tronstats.cpp:125-128), no marker (attn_stats.hpp:577-580).

(5) Defects a maintainer would block on, as committed: (a) compile break: t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:398-399 calls run_joins<geometry>(&q_batch, operation, output, 0, 2, true) with 6 args; the committed signature has 7 parameters, `bool stats_on` last with no default (self_attention.hpp:1170-1177); the file has no #if guards, and t_heterogeneous_scheduler is a fake-label test (t/CMakeLists.txt:581-583). (b) config/test-benchmarks.json has no t_attn_stats entry (grep count 0) while t/CMakeLists.txt:275 registers it; bin/slice bench --check exits 1 on missing_everywhere (bin/slice:1812-1820, 1836-1837) in the "Build Tron" job (.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml:483-485). (c) first-wins registration `if (fuse::stats::get_file_handle(prefix + "/summary")) return;` (attn_stats.hpp:596): runtron builds one scheduler per stream_generate call with the same cfg.id (stream_generate.hpp:915, destroyed at :1009, loop over batches and isolated iterations :1453-1466), so from the second batch on the leaves' weak_ptr is expired and every read returns "{}"; make_file returns the existing handle when read_only matches (src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:150-157) and set_read_callback replaces the callback (:987-995), so last-wins is the correct rule and needs no new code. (d) attn_stats.hpp:482 reads hardware::system::detail::cpu_frequency_hz, the only reader of that detail:: symbol outside h/system and src/system; no public accessor exists (system.hpp:245-254 has only the extern in namespace detail). (e) attn_stats.hpp:126-128 states the wrong kill-switch identity ("With TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 this equals the AMX-on run's amx visits"); fresh full pages are AVX even with AMX on (is_dense_amx_page needs the whole page inside one range, HEAD :1605-1616; fresh pages have one range per token, :1493-1494), so kill-switch avx_full_page_visits == AMX-on (amx_visits + avx_full_page_visits), and only for identical token streams. (f) T4 keeps plain non-atomic state in model_stats (t4_last_operation, t4_last_layer, t4_layer_start_cycles, attn_stats.hpp:231-234) written by worker 0 and reset by the main thread in begin_forward; correct only because forwards are serialized (llama.hpp:710 workers_done.wait, work_queue single thread), a subtlety reviewers will question. (g) `stats->on` is two dependent loads per call (shared_ptr then bool).

Verdict: env var, with the per-visit hooks kept as plain `if` gates, the fallback (per-visit hooks only behind a CMake option) triggered solely by the acceptance test below, and the PR cut to the items the reviewers asked for so the hot-loop diff stays at 14 lines.

judges.reasoning:
Words used here: a visit = one apply_page_tok call, that is one (query token, KV page, KV head) triple; off state = the branch binary with the environment variable TRON_ATTN_STATS unset; band = the run-to-run spread of the same binary measured twice; TPS = generated tokens per second per user; step = one decode forward for all users.

Verdict: one environment variable for every counter and timer, including the per-visit tallies. The off-state cost of the per-visit hook is not obvious by any measure available, and the margin to an obvious loss is two to three orders of magnitude. The pending A/A run is the gate; it flips the decision only under the condition named in the acceptance test.

Off-state cost of the committed hook shape (worktree commit 9b3832eb4b on main 66c7bb8db1):
- Per apply_page_range call: two dependent loads (shared_ptr pointer, then the bool) [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1439], zeroing a 64-byte stack object (8 x uint64, n_visits included) [:1440; h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:123-130], and one test at the end [:1631]. That is about 5-10 cycles per call.
- Per visit: one test of a register or stack bool [:1601]. The path value is a compile-time constant at each of the three return sites [:1849, :1901, :1933] and apply_page_tok is always_inline [:1790; h/common/attributes.hpp:24, :78], so after inlining the compiler either threads the test into each return path or keeps one byte phi. Either form is 1-2 cycles off the compute dependency chain. Nothing touches memory when off. The 16-byte struct return never crosses a call boundary (nm on the 8fd1e7798d binary: 0 apply_page_tok symbols, 472 apply_page_range instantiations).
- Sizing (computed with a script from the design page's unit costs, single-attn-20260901 summary.json: AMX 2.14-2.38 us per dense visit at prompt 1024, 2.89 us at 8192): qwen-3-4b tp2 8 users runs 42,624 visits per step at prompt 1024 (step 12.66 ms) and 300,672 at prompt 8192 (step 58.7 ms). At 2 cycles per visit and 2.7-3.9 GHz that is 0.6-2.4 us per worker per step at prompt 1024 and 4-17 us at prompt 8192, i.e. 0.003-0.03 % of the step for 13-27 attention workers. A 1 % TPS loss would need 116-465 added cycles per dense visit (attention share est. 20-50 %, unverified: n_attn_workers of the our-half placement is not in the repo).

How the cost report and its refutation weigh in:
- The report's core claim (one predictable branch per visit, no memory traffic, no atomics when off) holds against the committed code. Its fetch_add warning is already honored: add_relaxed is load + add + store [attn_stats.hpp:107-110], and add_visits skips empty tallies [:299-303].
- The refutation corrected details without changing the verdict: stats->on is two loads not one; the tally is 64 bytes not 56; the per-seed and struct-order details were fixed in the commit (pointer-first, static_assert at self_attention.hpp:1779-1782). Its one substantive cost point is on the ON path: note_token_path does two bounds checks on a vector<vector<uint8_t>> per visit, and the char-typed store forces reloads of this->stats and the vector bounds each visit [attn_stats.hpp:289-293]. That costs only when the switch is on and is fixed by hoisting a span per call (design change 1).
- Precedent cuts both ways. Compile-time: TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS [CMakeLists.txt:47] and TRON_MWAIT_STATS [src/system/CMakeLists.txt:36], both added this month, both in hot paths. Always-compiled and run-time gated: the perfetto TRACE_EVENT at the top of every apply_page_range call (a category check per call), the 8 unconditional rdtsc reads per attention job [self_attention.hpp:763-806 at HEAD], and FUSE stats (ENABLE_FUSE_STATS default ON, CMakeLists.txt:45). The convention argument for a build option is therefore not a measured cost argument.
- What the A/A can and cannot certify: the same-binary band at prompt 1024 is about 0.62 TPS = 0.8 % (Step E 2026-09-22, sd 0.28-0.35 TPS, 3 reps); detecting a 0.1 % shift would need about 250 reps per arm. The A/A certifies "not obvious" (no loss beyond about 0.5-0.8 %), which is exactly the user's rule. The "< 0.1 %" statement rests on the instruction count, so the acceptance test adds perf stat and an objdump check as deterministic cross-checks.

Why not option (2) now: a CMake option around the per-visit tallies buys a byte-identical production binary at the price of a second switch, two code shapes in every one of the 472 instantiations, and no AMX/AVX split in the deb that CI runs under platformd. That price is justified only if the hot loop's code generation regressed, which the acceptance test would show as a loss beyond 0.5 % in both cells. Shipping the option preemptively is speculative.

Residual risk (why 0.85 and not higher): register pressure in the always_inline hot loop is a code-generation question; stats_on must stay live across the page loop, and the served byte adds one phi. The objdump and perf stat checks in the acceptance test close this. Unverified: rdtsc cost on 3bda (31 ticks measured on the AMD claude-box), core clock under AMX load, n_attn_workers on our half.

State of the gate: the chain is running on 3bda (pid 2080049, head configure done 18:33:33 UTC) with the right arms and cells [exec/attnstats-20260924/chain.sh]. Its decide.py flip rule needs the relative floor named below; without it a 0.2 % drift at prompt 8192 (sd 0.01-0.02 TPS) can produce a false flip.
judges.acceptance_test:
Measurement M1 (the switch gate), on our half of delphi-3bda (socket 1, --instance 2,4), runtron stream-generate-text, model ingested-qwen-3-4b-instruct-2507-tp2 (36 layers, 8 KV heads, head 128, kv_mul 4: AMX-eligible), 8 users, 256 generated tokens per user (--dont-stop), CPU attention (USE_HW_ATTN=0), AMX on (TRON_AMX_DISABLE unset), hugepage file, two cells: prompt 1024 and prompt 8192. Arms: base = main 66c7bb8db1 (runtron.attnbase); head = branch 9b3832eb4b with TRON_ATTN_STATS unset (the off state); base2 = main again (same-binary control); headon = branch with TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 (on-state cost, informational only). Three repetitions per (cell, arm), interleaved rep-major (for rep, for cell, for arm) as exec/attnstats-20260924/campaign.sh does. Metric: decode TPS per user, mean of 3 and sample sd; TTFT recorded but not a gate.

Band per cell: B = max(|mean(base2) - mean(base)|, 2 x max(sd_base, sd_head), 0.5 % of mean(base)). Expected: B about 0.62 TPS (0.8 %) at prompt 1024 and about 0.09 TPS (0.5 %) at prompt 8192.

Host validity: |mean(base2) - mean(base)| <= 2 x max(sd_base, sd_base2) in both cells; otherwise the cell is rerun before any verdict.

Pass (environment variable stays): mean(head) >= mean(base) - B in both cells.

Flip (build option for the per-visit tallies only, env var for the rest): mean(head) < mean(base) - B in BOTH cells (a loss beyond the band and beyond 0.5 %, same sign at both prompt lengths). One cell only: add 3 repetitions to that cell; flip if the loss persists there and the other cell moves in the same direction.

Deterministic cross-checks, run after the TPS arms finish (never concurrently with a timed run): (a) perf stat -e instructions,cycles -p <engine pid> over one prompt-1024 run per arm (base, head off); expected instruction delta about 2-4 instructions x 42,624 visits = 0.09-0.17 M instructions per step; a delta above 20 instructions per visit means the compiler restructured the loop and the objdump must be read before deciding. (b) objdump -d of runtron.attnbase versus runtron.attnhead: the count of lock-prefixed instructions inside apply_page_range instantiations is unchanged; one hot instantiation grows by at most about 128 bytes; no new store instructions inside the dotter loop on the off path. (c) headon versus head gives the on-state cost; report it with its band, it does not affect the switch decision.

The 0.5 % floor is the "obvious" threshold: the computed off-state cost is 0.003-0.03 % of a step, so any real loss beyond 0.5 % can only come from a hot-loop code-generation change, which is the one case where a byte-identical production binary (build option) is worth a second switch.

(3) With a build option the counting binary is a different binary from the one whose TPS is under test, so the same-binary pair design of p0perf-20260911 / i4525-20260922 (kill switch vs on on one binary) is lost for every counted cell.
